title: The Serpent Power: being the Shat-chakra-nirupana and Paduka-panchaka
author: Purnananda Svami (Shat-chakra-nirupana, 1577) with Kalicharana's commentary; introduction by Arthur Avalon (Sir John Woodroffe)
edition_cited: Second revised edition, Madras: Ganesh & Co., 1924 (archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.283748, Digital Library of India scan; OCR is noisy)
tradition: Bengali Shakta tantra, laya / kundalini yoga
locator_hints: Shat-chakra-nirupana verse 36 with commentary (file lines c. 20105-20175): 'When the Yogi closes the house which hangs without support ... he then sees ... sparks of fire distinctly shining'; commentary identifies the closing as Yoni-mudra and quotes its definition (heels, crow-beak inhalation, thumbs on ears, index fingers on eyes, middle fingers on nostrils, breath restrained)
Verse 37 with commentary (file lines c. 20240-20300): 'After seeing the fiery sparks they see the light', a light like the morning sun glowing 'between the Sky and the Earth'
Verses 32-35: the Ajna lotus, the inner Atma 'lustrous like a flame', sparks surrounding (file lines c. 19800-20100, 20595)

Introduction, section on practice, printed pp. 223-224 (file lines c. 11040-11135): the Gheranda samadhi types; rasananda yoga by closing both ears with kumbhaka, 'the Anahata sound is heard, and the Light (Jyotih) ... is seen'; Shanmukhi mudra and stages of nada
Introduction: search 'Shambhavi', 'Trataka', 'Jyotirdhyana' for Woodroffe's summaries of the hatha practices
summary: Woodroffe's translation of Purnananda's sixteenth-century description of the chakras with Kalicharana's commentary. Verses 36-37 on the ajna centre describe a sequence: the yogi 'closes the house', which the commentator reads as Yoni-mudra and defines in detail (left heel at the anus, right heel on the left foot, air drawn in through crow-beak lips, ears closed by thumbs, eyes by index fingers, nostrils by middle fingers, mouth by the rest, breath held, attention on the pranava at the brow); when the mind dissolves there by repeated practice, sparks of fire are seen distinctly shining in the space above; after the sparks comes a steady light like the morning sun. The knowledge is said to be gained through service of the guru. Woodroffe's long introduction also summarises ear-closing with retention leading to inner sound and then seen light, and Shanmukhi mudra.
why_relevant: A tantric text and commentary giving a two-stage sign sequence (sparks, then steady light) tied to an explicitly described sense-closure technique.
